H2 — 4. Execution Risk: Leg Risk and Liquidation

Delta-Neutral # No-Risk

Leg Risk (One-Leg Execution Failure)

You successfully buy the spot, but due to slippage,
RPC latency, or DEX liquidity shifts, the short future
execution fails. The spread vanishes, leaving you
holding naked directional risk.

Liquidation Risk (Collateral Exposure)

lf the asset price suddenly doubles, your short
position requires massive margin. Even if the spot leg
is equally profitable, the short position may face
forced liquidation if sufficient collateral is unavailable
on that specific venue.
